Package com.robojacks.lib.input

Class VexController

java.lang.Object
com.robojacks.lib.input.VexController
public class VexController extends Object
Like WPILib's CommandXboxController, for the V5 controller: buttons are Triggers you bind commands to, sticks are -1 to 1, and you can write to the controller's screen and rumble it. 

 private final VexController m_driverController = new VexController(0);   // primary
 private final VexController m_operatorController = new VexController(1); // partner

 m_driverController.r1().whileTrue(m_intake.runCommand());
 m_driverController.axisMagnitudeGreaterThan(VexController.Axis.kRightX, 0.1)
         .whileTrue(m_turret.manualCommand(m_driverController::getRightX));
 m_driverController.setText(0, 0, "Auto: " + m_autoSelector.getSelectedName());

NOTE: axes keep VEX's signs: stick UP is POSITIVE (FRC joysticks are the opposite), stick RIGHT is positive. So "forward = getLeftY()" with no minus sign.

    • setText

      public void setText(int line, int column, String text)
      Writes text on the controller's screen. Line 0-2, column 0-18 (19 characters fit). Updates are sent about every 50 ms, the fastest VEXos accepts; the latest text wins.

    • rumble

      public void rumble(String pattern)
      Rumbles the controller. Pattern: '.' short buzz, '-' long buzz, ' ' pause; up to 8 symbols, e.g. "..-".
